provider: EPrints 3.x platform class (White Rose, QUT, Southampton)

free_tier.stated: No quota model. EPrints has no per-user or per-collection byte accounting; the only constraints are the JavaScript max on the upload widget and Apache's LimitRequestBody.

egress.terms: Direct, no CDN in front on the instances checked.

tooling: SWORD client / curl POST to cgi/
chaining: Structurally unbounded, but the write gate is deposit-medated: White Rose's own registration page tells depositors to go through their university's CRIS (Symplectic, PURE, myPublications) instead of registering.
limits_note: Per-file only, set by Apache LimitRequestBody or the form's JS; practitioners on the EPrints list cite successful 50 GB uploads and advise against >10 GB because there is no resumable upload.
reliability_note: No resumable upload and no failure recovery — a >10 GB POST that drops must restart from zero.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.

evidence.proved: 200; 'To deposit an item you do not normally need to register here. Instead, please follow the appropriate link from the list below: University of Leeds staff via Symplectic Elements ... Sheffield ... myPublications ... York ... PURE'
'We have had successful uploads of files of up to 50GB in the past'
'I would normally advise against using EPrints for files larger than 10GB ... there is no in-built failure recovery'
